STRATEGIC BRIEFING: MODEL BEHAVIORAL ANALYSIS (CAMPAIGN 1901-1910)

This briefing outlines the behavioral patterns and strategic tendencies of the opponent models encountered during the 1901-1910 campaign. Use this to calibrate your diplomacy and military planning in future games, regardless of the power you control.

MODEL PROFILES

anthropic/claude-opus-4.6 (The High-Fidelity Executioner)
Behavior: Extremely reliable in coordination and execution, but possesses a "zero-tolerance" policy for betrayal. Opus is the gold standard for complex, multi-turn maneuvers (e.g., the "Fork" strategy to dismantle Austria). However, once a trust bond is broken, the transition from ally to predator is instantaneous and total.
Tactics: Precise unit management and high-strength coordination. When allied, they provide the exact support promised. When hostile, they strike with overwhelming force and efficiency.
Advice: Prioritize an alliance with Opus; they are the most capable partner for dismantling superpowers. However, never treat a promise to Opus lightly. A single failed move (as seen with the A ALB -> CON failure) can trigger a catastrophic collapse of the alliance.

openai/gpt-5.4 (The Vacuum Predator)
Behavior: Fundamentally deceptive. GPT-5.4 uses the language of "neutrality," "restraint," and "DMZs" as a psychological mask to lull opponents into a false sense of security. They do not seek stability; they seek vacuums.
Tactics: The "Fortress" Strategy. Once they occupy a center, they build a high-strength defensive shell. In this game, a strength-3 defense in Warsaw rendered a strength-3 attack useless, resulting in a bounce. They aggressively occupy any province the moment it is vacated or contested.
Advice: Zero Trust Policy. Never believe a promise of "restraint" if they have units poised to strike. Do not attempt solo probes or parity attacks against their positions; only a strength-4 or 5 strike can break a GPT-5.4 fortress. Assume any "neutral" stance is a preparation for an opportunistic strike.

x-ai/grok-4.1-fast (The Volatile Saboteur)
Behavior: High volatility and low reliability. Grok views agreements as temporary conveniences rather than commitments. They are prone to sudden betrayals and active attempts to sow discord between other allied powers.
Tactics: Deceptive positioning and "kamikaze" strikes. Grok violated the Armenia DMZ early and fundamentally betrayed a critical support agreement in Romania (F1903), leading to a failed offensive.
Advice: Treat Grok as a tactical tool, not a strategic partner. Never rely on their support for a critical maneuver. Use them to distract other powers, but always maintain a defensive posture on your shared border.

deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (The Resilient Turtle)
Behavior: Methodical and defensive. DeepSeek excels at creating "Fortress" zones that are incredibly difficult to crack without external coordination.
Tactics: Overlapping supports. They held Serbia and Greece for years by ensuring every center was supported by another, forcing the opponent to commit massive resources for a single gain.
Advice: Do not waste units on solo probes. To defeat DeepSeek, you must coordinate a multi-power strike. The only way to break their line in this game was a coordinated strength-3 attack with Italy.

qwen/qwen3.5-27b & qwen3.6-plus (The Opportunistic Pressurers)
Behavior: Proactive and aggressive, though less focused on long-term "fortresses" than GPT-5.4. They use diplomatic pressure and threats to secure concessions.
Tactics: Direct territorial demands and flanking maneuvers. England (Qwen) maintained a hostile posture and demanded the return of centers (NWY) to pressure the northern flank.
Advice: Use Qwen's aggression to your advantage by directing them toward other threats. They are susceptible to being distracted by larger conflicts.

CORE STRATEGIC LESSONS

1. The Fallacy of the "Hold" Order
In contested zones, a "Hold" order is an invitation to be dislodged. Against aggressive models like GPT-5.4 and Claude-Opus, passive defense is a failure. If you are not actively supporting or attacking, you are creating a vacuum. Always use active moves or supports to maintain a presence in high-risk areas.

2. Breaking the "Fortress"
Parity is a failure. Against "Fortress" players (DeepSeek, GPT-5.4), a strength-3 attack against a strength-3 defense results in a bounce and total stagnation. To achieve a breakthrough, you must achieve a strength-4 or 5 advantage. This requires absolute synchronization with an ally.

3. The Vacuum Effect
The "Vacuum Effect" is most prominent with GPT-5.4. The moment a unit moves out of a province or a DMZ is proposed, the model will attempt to occupy the space. Never vacate a strategic province unless you have a guaranteed move to retake it or a strong defensive line immediately behind it.

4. The Reliability Paradox
While Claude-Opus is the most reliable in terms of order execution, this reliability makes the consequences of a betrayal more severe. A "reliable" ally is a more dangerous enemy because they know exactly how to dismantle your position.

ACTIONABLE CHECKLIST FOR FUTURE GAMES
- If allied with Opus: Execute every promise with 100% accuracy.
- If bordering GPT-5.4: Ignore all "restraint" agreements; maintain military deterrence.
- If coordinating with Grok: Assume the support order will not be placed.
- If attacking a "Fortress": Coordinate a strength-4+ strike; do not probe.
- General: Avoid "Hold" orders in any province adjacent to an enemy unit.
final_goals: Defend Constantinople and the Anatolian heartland from Italian aggression
Contain Germany's expansion in the East and prevent the loss of UKR
Maintain the non-aggression pact with France in the Mediterranean
Stabilize borders to prevent further supply center losses before attempting to reclaim WAR
